provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: The human reproductive system
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state physical changes during adolescence.
The pupils should be able to explain responsible living choices.

Introduction:
We have learned about body systems in previous lessons.
Today we will discuss changes that happen as we grow up.

Content:
Adolescence is when children become young adults.
Boys and girls experience different changes like hair growth and voice changes.
Responsible living means making good choices for our health.
We should respect our bodies and others as we grow.

Class activity:
Pupils will list changes they expect during adolescence in groups.

Evaluation questions:
What is adolescence?
Name one change boys experience.
How can we show responsible living?

Summary:
Adolescence brings physical changes and we must make healthy choices.

topics.title: The nervous system
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the main parts of the nervous system.
The pupils should be able to explain how nerves carry messages.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about body changes during adolescence.
Today we will explore how our body controls actions and feelings.

Content:
The nervous system has the brain, spinal cord and nerves.
The brain is like the computer of the body.
Nerves carry messages like electrical wires.
When you touch a hot pot, nerves send quick messages to your brain.

Class activity:
Pupils will play a reaction game where they catch a ruler dropped by a partner.

Evaluation questions:
Name two parts of the nervous system.
How do nerves work like electrical wires?
What happens when you touch something hot?

Summary:
The nervous system helps us react quickly to things around us.

topics.title: The circulatory system
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the parts of the circulatory system.
The pupils should be able to measure their pulse rate.

Introduction:
We learned how nerves help us react to things.
Today we will learn how blood moves through our body.

Content:
The circulatory system has the heart, blood vessels and blood.
The heart pumps blood like a water pump in our community.
Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to all parts of the body.
We can feel our pulse where blood vessels are close to the skin.

Class activity:
Pupils will measure their pulse rate at the wrist and count beats for 30 seconds.

Evaluation questions:
What is the main organ of the circulatory system?
What does blood carry in our body?
Where can you feel your pulse?

Summary:
The circulatory system moves blood to keep our body working well.

topics.title: The respiratory system
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name the main parts of the respiratory system.
The pupils should be able to explain why clean air is important.

Introduction:
Last week we learned how blood moves through our body.
Today we will explore how we breathe and why clean air matters.

Content:
The respiratory system includes the nose, windpipe and lungs.
Air enters through the nose like water through a pipe.
Lungs help oxygen enter the blood and remove carbon dioxide.
In harmattan season, dirty air can make breathing hard for some people.

Class activity:
Pupils will make a simple lung model using a plastic bottle and balloons.

Evaluation questions:
Name two parts of the respiratory system.
What happens when we breathe in?
Why is clean air important for our health?

Summary:
The respiratory system helps us breathe and we need clean air to stay healthy.

topics.title: The digestive system
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the organs of digestion in order.
The pupils should be able to explain healthy eating habits.

Introduction:
We learned about breathing and clean air last week.
Today we will discover how our body breaks down food for energy.

Content:
The digestive system includes the mouth, stomach and intestines.
Food enters through the mouth like water entering a pipe.
The stomach breaks down food using acids like a local market grinding machine.
Healthy eating means eating fruits, vegetables and less fatty foods.

Class activity:
Pupils will create a poster showing the path of food through the digestive system.

Evaluation questions:
Name one organ in the digestive system.
What does the stomach do to food?
Why is eating fruits and vegetables important?

Summary:
The digestive system breaks down food to give us energy for daily activities.

topics.title: Drugs and health
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to differentiate between drug use and misuse.
The pupils should be able to state ways to say no to drug abuse.

Introduction:
We learned how our body digests food last week.
Today we will learn about drugs and how they can affect our health.

Content:
Drugs are substances that change how our body works.
Some drugs like malaria medicine help us when used correctly.
Drug misuse is using drugs the wrong way or without permission.
We can say no to drugs by talking to adults and joining sports activities.

Class activity:
Pupils will role-play saying no to peer pressure to try drugs.

Evaluation questions:
What is the difference between drug use and misuse?
Name one way to say no to drug abuse.
Why is it important to use medicine correctly?

Summary:
Drugs can help us when used properly but misuse can harm our health.

topics.title: Food processing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list three food preservation methods.
The pupils should be able to explain why we preserve food.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about drugs and their effects on health.
Today we will discover how we can keep food from spoiling.

Content:
Food processing changes food to make it last longer.
Preservation methods include drying, salting and smoking fish.
We preserve food to have enough during the dry season when farming is hard.
Our grandparents used to dry pepper and fish to sell at the market.

Class activity:
Pupils will demonstrate how to dry mango slices using the sun.

Evaluation questions:
Name one method of food preservation.
Why do we preserve food?
What happens if food is not preserved?

Summary:
Food processing helps us store food for when fresh food is not available.

topics.title: Simple machine review
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different types of simple machines.
The pupils should be able to explain how simple machines make work easier.

Introduction:
We learned about preserving food last week.
Today we will review simple machines that help us in daily life.

Content:
Simple machines include levers, pulleys and gears.
A lever is like a seesaw or a wheelbarrow used in the market.
Pulleys help lift heavy loads like water from a well.
Gears help machines work together like the parts of a bicycle.

Class activity:
Pupils will build a simple machine model using materials like cardboard and strings.

Evaluation questions:
Name two types of simple machines.
How does a lever make work easier?
Where can you find gears in everyday objects?

Summary:
Simple machines help us do work with less effort in our daily activities.

topics.title: Electricity projects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how a series circuit works.
The pupils should be able to construct a simple torch.

Introduction:
Last week we reviewed simple machines that help us work easier.
Today we will explore electricity and how to make a simple torch.

Content:
Electricity flows through circuits like water through pipes.
A series circuit has only one path for electricity to flow.
When we connect a battery, bulb and switch, we make a complete circuit.
In Nigeria, we experience power cuts so making a torch is useful.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to make a simple torch using a battery, bulb and wires.

Evaluation questions:
What is a series circuit?
Name three parts needed to make a torch.
Why is it important to know how circuits work?

Summary:
Electricity flows through circuits and we can make useful devices like torches.

topics.title: Revision and project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall key concepts from term one.
The pupils should be able to present their completed project.

Introduction:
This week we will review what we learned this term.
We will also show the projects we made in class.

Content:
We learned about body systems like the nervous and circulatory systems.
We discussed drugs, food processing and simple machines.
Our projects included making torches and simple machine models.
These skills help us understand how things work around us.

Class activity:
Pupils will present their projects to the class and explain how they work.

Evaluation questions:
Name one body system we learned about.
What did you learn about food preservation?
How does your simple machine make work easier?

Summary:
This term we learned about our body, health and simple machines that help us in daily life.
